summary: Mio Kishimoto is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1979) and held posts at Ochanomizu University (~1979–1994) and the University of Tokyo (~1994–2007).
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, teacher Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Mircea Eliade was a scholar of religion, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his PhD at the University of Bucharest under Nae Ionescu, studied at Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta, and held professorships at the Sorbonne and the University of Chicago.

Mireille Helffer was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She was a Chargé de Recherche at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (~1961–1993) and held a post at Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).
Mirella Lingorska works in Indology and linguistics. She held posts at the University of Tübingen and as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi at the University of Zurich, both attested in 2026.

Miri Albahari works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary under John A. Baker, later holding posts at New South Wales and Western Australia.

Miriam Levering was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 1978 and served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška studied law at Zagreb, the Hague Academy, the International Faculty of Comparative Law, and Ljubljana (PhD 1960). He held posts at the University of Zagreb, University of Pennsylvania, and Yale University (beginning 1975–1976).
Mitchell G. Weiss is an Indologist who studied under Ludo Rocher and served as a professor at the University of Basel.

Mithilesh Chaturvedi is a scholar in Indology and linguistics affiliated with the University of Delhi's Department of Sanskrit (attested 2009) and later recognized as Professor emeritus there (attested 2026).

Mitsuji Fukunaga was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and religion. He studied at Kyoto University, later serving on its faculty (1947, 1961–1982), and held professorships at the University of Tokyo, Kansai University, and the University of Kitakyushu.
Mitsukuni Yoshida was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1941–1945) and later held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts (~1985–1991).
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University, where he also served as a lecturer (attested 1989–1995).
Mitsuyo Demoto is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and held an affiliation at the University of Marburg (attested 2024).

Mitsuyoshi Saegusa was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned doctorates from Munich and Kokugakuin, and held teaching posts at Tokyo, Kokugakuin, Tsukuba, and Nihon University, as well as head of the Eastern Institute.

Mitsuyuki Ishida was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later taught at Ryukoku University (attested 1956, 1976 as professor) and served as a professor at Shitennoji University (attested 1976).
Miyako Notake is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who has served as a part-time lecturer at Waseda University (attested 2015 and 2026).
Miyoko Nakano is a sinologist who studied at Hokkaido University (~1952–1956) and later held an academic post there (~1970–1996).

Mizuho Okita is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at Tokai University, under Katsuhiko Kamimura, and earned her doctorate under Atsuhiko Yoshida at Gakushuin University, later lecturing at Meisei University (attested 2008).
